annotations.description: Last commit to lakehouse.events was 10m 15s ago.
annotations.summary: The events table has not received a commit for over 5 minutes

diagnosis.summary: IcebergTableStale was caused by a simultaneous restart of all 3 Kafka brokers ~18 min ago (exit_code 255/Unknown, likely a chaos-mesh experiment), which crashed the Flink job and halted Iceberg commits. The Flink job has since restarted and recovered — 19 checkpoints completed in the last 5 min, consumer lag 0, and lakehouse.events received a commit just 1.9 min ago. The alert should clear imminently.
diagnosis.root_cause: All three Kafka brokers (lakehouse-dual-role-0/1/2) terminated simultaneously ~18.8 min ago with exit_code 255/Unknown, causing all dependent services (ingestion, iceberg-exporter, Flink job) to crash at the same time. This stopped Iceberg checkpoints for ~15 minutes. The chaos-mesh-local app was deployed ~110 min ago and there were two identical disruption waves (~51 min ago and ~18 min ago), strongly suggesting a scheduled chaos experiment. All components self-healed: Kafka brokers restarted within ~1 min, and the Flink job recovered ~3.6 min ago. Iceberg commits resumed 1.9 min ago.
diagnosis.impact: No new events were visible to downstream query tools (Athena/Spark) for approximately 15 minutes around the alert window. No data was lost — events remained in Kafka and were committed once Flink resumed. A second earlier disruption ~51 min ago also caused a brief outage with Kubernetes API/configmap sync failures.

evidence.finding: Only LakehouseReconciliationStale (warning, firing 1.7 min) remains. IcebergTableStale (critical) is the subject alert.
Flink job RUNNING/STABLE, started 3.6 min ago. 19 completed checkpoints in last 5 min, 0 failed checkpoints, last checkpoint 97ms, consumer lag 0, 0 restarts in last 15 min.

All 3 brokers Running/Ready. All 3 had last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 finished_minutes_ago=18.8 — simultaneous crash. 0 under-replicated/offline partitions now. Consumer lag for flink-events-to-iceberg=0.
lakehouse.events last_commit_minutes_ago=1.9 — table is fresh again. However 146/146 data files are small files; last compaction 1.7 hours ago.

chaos-mesh-local deployed 110.4 min ago (revision 2.8.5,7d448a789610) and again 203.3 min ago. platform-local also redeployed at the same time. Two disruption waves followed: ~51 min ago and ~18 min ago.

kafka namespace: all 3 brokers (dual-role-0/1/2) had readiness probe failures at 17.5-18.3 min ago; Strimzi operator and entity-operator also failed at same time. At ~50-51 min ago, another identical wave.

apps namespace: at ~18-19 min ago ingestion-service, iceberg-exporter, and Flink job manager all crashed simultaneously. At ~51 min ago, FailedMount errors 'failed to sync configmap/secret cache: timed out waiting for the condition' — indicating a brief Kubernetes API disruption.
All apps pods now Running/Ready. ingestion-service pods show 29/39 restarts with last termination ~18 min ago. iceberg-exporter has 7 restarts. Flink pods all show age ~4 min, 0 restarts.

proposed_action.rationale: The system has fully self-healed: Kafka brokers are healthy, Flink job is running with 19 successful checkpoints, consumer lag is 0, and Iceberg commits have resumed (last commit 1.9 min ago). The IcebergTableStale alert will clear on its own. No stuck or wedged pods require restarts.

follow_ups: Investigate whether chaos-mesh-local experiment (deployed ~110 min ago) deliberately triggered the simultaneous broker kill at ~18 and ~51 min ago. If not intentional, disable or reschedule the chaos experiment to avoid production impact.
lakehouse.events has 146/146 data files flagged as small files. Run iceberg compaction (run_iceberg_compaction on lakehouse.events) to address small-file build-up from repeated Flink restarts.
LakehouseReconciliationStale alert is still firing — the reconciliation table (lakehouse.events_reconciliation) has not been committed to in ~28 hours; investigate the reconciliation job separately.

Two disruption waves occurred (~51 min and ~18 min ago) with identical failure signatures. Confirm whether these are part of a scheduled chaos test or indicate an underlying instability (e.g., node memory pressure, network blip).

The FailedMount errors at ~51 min ago ('failed to sync configmap cache: timed out waiting for condition') suggest the Kubernetes API server was briefly unresponsive. Check API server metrics around that time.

{"results":[{"runbook":"docs/runbooks/pipeline.md#icebergtablestale","title":"Runbook: streaming pipeline (Kafka to Flink to Iceberg)","heading":"IcebergTableStale","text":"**Meaning:** no commit to `lakehouse.events` for over 5 minutes. The Flink sink commits on every checkpoint (every 10 s), even with no new data, so a stale table means checkpoints are not completing or the job is down.
**Impact:** queries (Athena, Spark) see no new data; the freshness SLO is being spent.
**Diagnose:**

1. Is the job running? `kc -n apps get flinkdeployment events-to-iceberg -o jsonpath='{.status.jobStatus.state}'` (see FlinkJobNotRunning).
2. Are checkpoints completing? Pipeline dashboard, "Checkpoints" panel (see FlinkCheckpointsStalled).
3. Can the job reach the catalog and storage? In Loki: `{namespace="apps", app="events-to-iceberg"} |= "Exception"`.
**Fix:** follow the alert that explains the cause. Data is not lost while the table is stale: events wait in Kafka and are committed once checkpoints resume."}]}
